title: Throughput warranty and contractual remediation guidelines for Dedicated capacity
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Purpose: Propose a standardized set of warranty terms for Dedicated capacity throughput guarantees, a practical error budget model translated into contract credit math, and operational remediation guidelines tied to autoscaling and fleet controls. This ticket collates product, infra, and legal inputs and produces: a) SLA metrics and measurement windows, b) error-budget computation in throughput-seconds and credits, c) concrete autoscaling-to-credit mappings, and d) sample contract language for BDR/RevOps and Legal to vet.

Scope: Applies to Reserved GPU/Dedicated deployments (not Hosted ephemeral). Covers throughput guarantees at the tenant level (per-customer dedicated pool), incident classification for throughput degradation, evidence required for crediting, and customer notice/mitigation obligations. Excludes pricing negotiations and bespoke enterprise amendments (those will be handled by Sales with Legal hooks).
sla_definitions: SLA metric: Customer Throughput Availability (CTA) measured as percentage of observed committed throughput delivered over a 30-day calendar window. Committed throughput is defined in the contract as a target aggregate requests-per-minute or tokens-per-second capacity (example: 50k QPS-requests-min or 1.2M tokens/min). Measurement method: platform telemetry aggregates per-tenant delivered throughput in 1-minute buckets. Any 1-minute bucket below 50% of committed throughput is counted as a degraded minute. CTA = 1 - (degraded_minutes / total_minutes_in_window). Availability thresholds: 'Satisfactory' >= 99.5%, 'Degraded' 98.0% - 99.5%, 'Material Failure' < 98.0%. Measurement window and timezone are explicit in contract. Exclusions: scheduled maintenance windows with prior notice, agreed capacity changes, customer-side network outages (unless platform demonstrates no egress failure), and documented customer request patterns that exceed agreed rate limits without autoscale configuration.
error_budget_model: Error budget is expressed in throughput-minutes per 30-day window and maps directly to financial credit. Compute: committed_throughput_per_minute * 30 * window_days = budgeted_throughput_minutes. Degraded minutes consume error budget proportionally to the shortfall percentage (e.g., if committed 1,000 tokens/min and minute delivered 700 tokens, shortfall=300 tokens -> consumes 0.3 throughput-minutes). Credit tiers: For total consumed error_budget <= 1% => no credit. 1% < consumed <= 3% => 5% service credit applied to monthly Dedicated fee for that customer. 3% < consumed <= 10% => 15% credit. >10% => 30% credit plus mandatory remediation plan and escalated review. Credits are capped at monthly fee. Credits are computed against base Dedicated subscription fees only (not usage overage or third-party infra pass-throughs). The model includes a burn-rate signal for automated escalation: if weekly burn rate projection predicts >5% monthly consumption, ops automation triggers a canary scaling policy.
autoscaling_policy_integration: Autoscaling tie-ins: Autoscaler must expose two knobs to contracts: a) Min reserved capacity (baseline that cannot be auto-evicted) and b) Burst budget (ephemeral pool used during spikes). Autoscaling triggers for remediation: if observed throughput < 80% of committed for 5 consecutive 1-minute buckets, and error_budget_remaining > 0, system will attempt immediate horizontal scale-up within configured burst budget. If scale-up is constrained by capacity, platform will attempt policy fallback (regional spillover to compatible dedicated nodes or prioritized preemptible capacity). Contract triggers: Customers may opt into 'Auto-Remediate' mode where Redwood attempts burst-add and accepts resulting usage billing; opting out requires written approval and may change credit calculation (we do not apply credits if customer refused remediation options that could have restored throughput). Autoscaling metrics (scale events, capacity throttles, eviction events) must be included as evidence for any credit claim.
fleet_controls_and_fallbacks: Fleet controls: Define three hierarchical fallback tiers: 1) Local pool autoscale (same cluster), 2) Regional failover to matched instance families, 3) Cross-region failover with degraded latency SLOs. Contracts must declare acceptable fallback tier(s). Fallback visibility: Customers will see roll-forward logs in Console and a 'fallback reason' field in incident exports. Controlled degradations: If fallback to lower-performance instance families is used for >15 minutes, that time counts as degraded minutes for error budget unless customer pre-approved cross-tier fallback in contract. Emergency throttling: Platform may temporarily throttle lower-priority non-dedicated traffic to preserve Dedicated throughput; such throttles and their timestamps serve as mitigation evidence.
contract_language_draft: Clause: Throughput Warranty. Subject to the terms herein, Redwood warrants that during each monthly measurement window the Customer's Dedicated Throughput Availability (CTA) will be no less than 99.5% as measured by Redwood's standard telemetry. For the avoidance of doubt, CTA and measurement methodology are defined in Schedule A (Measurement and Evidence). If CTA falls below the thresholds in Schedule A, Customer shall be entitled to service credits calculated as set forth in Schedule B (Credit Table). Customer must notify Redwood of a claim within thirty (30) days of the end of the measurement window and provide requested telemetry. Redwood will review and validate the claim in accordance with the evidence standard in Schedule A. Except as expressly provided herein, credits are Customer's sole and exclusive remedy for throughput warranty failures and shall be applied as a credit against future Dedicated fees. Notwithstanding the foregoing, if CTA is below 98.0% for two consecutive measurement windows, Redwood will, at its election, provide either (i) a one-time refund equal to the monthly Dedicated fee for the affected month, or (ii) an agreed remediation project and a service credit not less than 30% of the monthly Dedicated fee.
acceptance_criteria: Draft SLA/Measurement Schedule (Schedule A) reviewed and accepted by Infra and SRE
Credit Table (Schedule B) numeric values validated against historical incidents and finance model
Automation: telemetry exports for per-tenant throughput in 1-minute buckets available to Customer support and audit for at least 90 days
Ops runbook documenting autoscale remediation actions and evidence collection completed
Legal review signoff on sample clause language and notice periods
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal beta): apply new SLA measurement to a subset of pilot customers on dedicated pools (Q1 2026)
Phase 2 (partner rollout): offer opt-in Auto-Remediate mode and updated contract templates to sales pipeline customers
Phase 3 (general availability): publish standardized contract language, console indicators for CTA and error budget, and automated credit grant workflow
Monitor first three months of GA for burn-rate behavior and adjust credit tier thresholds if systemic variance is observed
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Measurement noise from bursty workloads can inflate degraded_minutes. Mitigation: apply smoothing and minimum-request thresholds; exclude minute buckets below 10 requests to avoid spurious shortfalls.

Risk: Overly generous credits could be exploited during a platform upgrade window. Mitigation: clearly define scheduled maintenance windows and require advance notice for upgrades that change capacity characteristics.
Risk: Autoscale may fail due to cloud capacity shortages. Mitigation: provide pre-negotiated regional failover and communicate capacity reservation SLAs for enterprise customers.
Risk: Legal pushback on refund vs credit. Mitigation: keep a fallback clause for remediation project within Enterprise negotiations and limit refunds to material failures only.
